default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-418.title: Cheap-move (high price impact per contract) micro-break fade
E-418.hypothesis: When the recent price change per contract traded (Amihud impact) is high for the time of day, the book is thin and a few small market orders move the price a lot; a short-box break made then costs the pushers little and carries no conviction, and the liquidity providers who refill the book lean against it, so fade the break back into the box.

E-419.title: Yesterday settled at its VWAP micro-break fade
E-419.hypothesis: When yesterday closed near its own volume-weighted price, the day's buyers and sellers ended near break-even with no trapped inventory to unwind today; with no carry-over pressure, short-term box breaks are not fed by forced exits and the two-sided players fade them back into the box.

E-420.title: Failed-opening-drive day micro-break fade
E-420.hypothesis: When the price is back on the other side of the session open from the direction of the opening drive, the early initiative traders have been proved wrong and the day becomes two-sided: they exit into strength and weakness while responsive traders re-centre; short-box breaks on such days are absorbed, so fade them.

E-421.title: Dollar parked mid-box index break fade
E-421.hypothesis: If the mini dollar sits in the middle of its own recent box when the index breaks its box, there is no macro or foreign-flow push behind the index move (foreign flows move both markets at once); the break is local order-book noise that index market makers take back, so fade it.

E-422.title: Yesterday's range-midpoint poke fade
E-422.hypothesis: The midpoint of yesterday's high-low range is the fair price of yesterday's auction, and range traders rest orders there; a bar that comes from one side, trades through the midpoint and closes back on its side shows the resting orders absorbed the push, so trade away from the level.

E-423.title: Inside-morning-range afternoon micro-break fade
E-423.hypothesis: After the morning has set the session's working range, afternoon participants (lighter local flow before the US session) trade inside it against its edges; a short-box break that still sits inside the morning range is a rotation, not a new leg, and the morning-range players fade it.

E-424.title: Futures-only evening micro-break fade
E-424.hypothesis: Once the B3 cash-equity session and the settlement window are over, the index future trades without spot arbitrage flow or index-fund orders; what is left is day traders squaring positions in a thin book, so short-box breaks then are inventory noise that reverts; fade them.

E-425.title: Rotating-box micro-break fade
E-425.hypothesis: A box whose closes keep crossing its own midpoint is a two-sided auction in which both sides keep being filled; a break out of such a box is usually the last swing of the rotation hitting stops just outside, after which the rotation resumes, so fade the break.

E-426.title: Braided-EMA micro-break fade
E-426.hypothesis: When the 9- and 21-bar EMAs have crossed back and forth several times recently, the moving-average trend followers have been whipsawed and stopped repeatedly and nobody holds a trend position; a 15-minute box break then has no trend money behind it and fades back into the box.

E-427.title: Same-sign index and dollar day micro-break fade
E-427.hypothesis: The index and the dollar usually move in opposite directions because foreign flows drive both; on a day when both are up (or down) since the open by a clear margin, the two markets are driven by separate local flows instead of one persistent foreign flow, so index box breaks lack a lasting push and fade.
